newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end week higher.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end week higher.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed sharply higher after local investors and foreign funds continued on a week-long buying spree sparked by solid coporate earnings.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose 1.26 percent to end the week at 16,684.49 on above-average trading volume of 2.5 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB rose 1.28 percent, meanwhile, ending at 1,060.51 on a volume of 1.8 billion pesos.

Gainers included Banco de Colombia, which jumped up 2.85 percent in Bogota to close at 433 pesos per share. The bank, Colombia's second-largest, did even better in Medellin, where it closed up 3.32 percent at 436 pesos per share.

Brokers said buying in Banco de Colombia was partly fueled by speculation about the share price that will be set when Spain's Banco Central Hispano follows through, as expected, on plans to buy up to a 36 percent stake in the bank.

Other winners among banks included Banco de Bogota, which moved up 1.84 percent in Bogota to 6,610 pesos per share, and Bancoquia, which closed up a sharp 4.06 percent in Medellin at 2,950 pesos per share. Bancoquia is the financial arm of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, a favorite among foreign funds.

Brewing giant Bavaria, flagship of the Santo Domingo industrial group, gained 2.44 percent in Bogota to close at 6,910 pesos per share and tobacco company Coltabaco rose a steep 4.05 percent in Bogota to end at 3,850 pesos per share.
Dealers said the rise in Coltabaco stemmed from the fact that it was currently the least expensive company listed in Bogota or Medellin belonging to the Sindicato Antioqueno.
